newsitem.title: USA: Vermont Yankee saved -- for now.
newsitem.headline: Vermont Yankee saved -- for now.

text.p: The Vermont Senate, as expected, gave final approval late Thursday to a measure that opens the electric utility industry in the state to competition.
But in a surprise move, the Senate essentially tabled a provision which utilities said would force them to shut Vermont Yankee, the state's lone nuclear plant.
Central Vermont Public Service and Green Mountain Power Corp are the principal owners of Vermont Yankee.
Several amendments were considered before the final vote, including one that sets up an economic feasibility study to guage the effects of decommissioning the controversial nuclear plant.
The amendment passed despite the pleas of Sen. Elizabeth Ready, D-Addison, who argued that the delay would merely allow Vermont Yankee to continue to be subsidized in an otherwise competitive market.
But other senators, including the amendment's sponsor, Fred Ehrich, R-Bennington, argued successfully that forcing closure now could severely hurt the state's economy.
The final vote on the restructuring bill was 20-9. The bill now moves to the Vermont House, which is likely to pass it. Gov. Howard Dean said he would sign the Senate bill as amended.
